To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the epithelial Ca(2+)-channel TRPV6 is expressed at highest level in the apical domain in duodenal epithelial cells of laying hens.
TRPV6 is expressed in all intestinal segments of hens, and that TRPV6 expression in the kidney is restricted to the distal tubules, but extends to the proximal tubules.

TRPV6 is localised to the apical membrane of the intestinal and renal epithelium in laying hens, and that TRPV6 mRNA is expressed most abundantly in the duodena and jejunum, followed by the ileum, caeca and rectum.
In summary, our research is concerned with

calcium (re) absorption in the gastrointestinal (GI) tract and kidney, and we have identified the expression and localisation of the calcium transporter TRPV6 in the GI tract and kidney of laying chickens.
the expression of the epithelium Ca2+ channel, TRPV6, in the intestine and kidney of laying chickens.
the role of TRPV6 as a potential target for improving calcium (re) absorption, which is a major factor in the development of osteoporosis in laying hens and other animals.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the epithelial calcium channel TRPV6 plays an important role in calcium (re) absorption in the laying hens.
TRPV6 is a major component in Ca2+ translocation and that it is strongly expressed in all intestinal segments as well as the renal tubules in laying hens.
the epithelial Ca(2+) channel TRPV6 plays a crucial role during peak lay in dietary Ca(2+) (re)absorptive processes in laying hens.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
TRPV6 is expressed in the apicallateral membranes of all intestinal segments and the renal tubule of the laying hens and the expression is higher in duodenum and kidney.
TRPV6 plays an important role in calcium homeostasis and that the expression and localisation of TRPV6 is tissue and segment specific.
TRPV6 expression is highest in the duodenal epithelia of laying hens.
The main takeaway from our work is that

TRPV6, the epithelial calcium channel that is expressed in the apices of the intestinal epithelium and kidney tubules, is expressed throughout the entire intestine of laying hens and is also expressed in the kidney.
we have identified TRPV6 as a potential candidate for increasing the calcium uptake of laying hens.
TRPV6 is a key regulator of Ca2+ homeostasis and that its expression is highest in the duodenal epithelium.
